subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs for Finlytics
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs for Finlytics

Hi Sam / Priya 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps.

Key pain points you highlighted:
- High tail latency on inference for real-time scoring (~P95 > 500ms for 512-token prompts)
- Cost unpredictability at peak trading hours and batch vs real-time mix
- Need for deterministic throughput for SLA-backed customer offers

Goals we discussed:
- P95 inference latency target: <= 200ms for common 128-token requests; P99 budget of 500ms
- Baseline throughput: 200 qps sustained with headroom to spike to 800 qps during market open
- Multi-region failover and encryption at rest for regulated data

Technical constraints you called out:
- Must use 8-bit quantized transformer for cost targets; some models must keep FP16 for accuracy-sensitive flows
- KV cache reuse is critical for your conversation-based routing
- On-prem deployment will be considered for production-sensitive data in Q4

Actions / next steps:
1) Marissa to draft a sizing proposal (GPU types, cluster topology, estimated token cost)  by Tue 16 Mar
2) Aditya to share the Redwood Sizing Playbook and a mutual action plan spreadsheet (attached)
3) Schedule a follow-up to review model variant tradeoffs (quant vs FP16) and a canary rollout plan  propose Wed 17 Mar or Thu 18 Mar

Attachments: Redwood Sizing Playbook (PDF), Finlytics MAP (Excel)

If I missed anything, please flag. Thanks again  great conversation.

Best,

Subject: Re: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs for Finlytics

Hi Sam / Priya 

Follow-up from the technical side with more detail on tradeoffs we discussed: 

1) Latency targets & model choices:
- For P95 <= 200ms at 128 tokens we recommend a trimmed transformer variant (8-bit quant) served on A100-type or equivalent instances with optimized kernels.
- For the accuracy-sensitive scoring path (rules engine + human-in-the-loop), keep FP16 or mixed-precision and serve on higher-memory GPUs; this will be a small portion of traffic but needs different autoscaling.

2) Throughput & topology:
- Proposed baseline cluster: 4 dedicated inference workers (multi-GPU nodes) behind the Redwood routing tier with an autoscale buffer of +2 nodes for spikes. This gives ~200 qps sustained with target headroom.
- KV cache shard placement: colocate cache with the worker nodes serving session-heavy traffic to avoid network hop latency.

3) Canary/deployment:
- Canary policy: 5% traffic for 24 hours with rollback on latency/regression alerts.
- Instrumentation: token-level latency traces, per-route success/error rates, and per-model quality regression tests tied to your eval prompt set.

4) Cost levers:
- Batch windows for non-real-time scoring, and prefix caching for repeated context to reduce compute.
- We can estimate per-token cost in the sizing doc; initial rough number attached.

I attached a short sizing worksheet and a topology diagram link. Marcus and I can join the next call to walk through the GPU types and rollout steps.

Marissa

Thanks for the clear recap. That aligns with our takeaways. A couple quick clarifications: 
- Can you confirm expected P99 at baseline and under 3x traffic spikes? We need to model worst-case for compliance.
- For the FP16 path, what is expected autoscale cooldown and instance warm-up time? We have short-lived heavy bursts.

We're good to meet Wed 17 Mar 10:00 PT. Priya and I will review the sizing workbook before the call.

Sam

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs for Finlytics

Sam / Priya 

Short answers ahead of Wednesday: 
- P99 baselines: expect ~450ms at baseline for 128 tokens on the 8-bit config; under 3x spikes P99 could approach 900ms without autoscale buffer. With the +2 node burst policy we estimate P99 stays below 600ms. We'll put exact numbers in the sizing spreadsheet.
- FP16 autoscale/warm-up: instance spin-up ~90-120s; model cold-start (warm KV cache) can add ~150-300ms for first requests. For short bursts we recommend predictive pre-warming and keeping a small pool of warmed FP16 nodes during market open windows.

I'll bring a short slide with the topology and a canary checklist to Wed 17 Mar 10:00 PT.

Thanks 
Marcus Lin
